rule: GOAL: Align the yellow knob with the gap in the black bar to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click the top blue button to shift the upper boundary left; click the bottom blue button to shift the lower boundary right. RULE: The boundary acts like a rigid zigzag line, so moving one segment forces the other to move in the opposite direction to maintain connection. TRAP: Assuming the segments move independently or in the same direction, which wastes moves trying to force alignment without respecting the linked motion.

GOAL: Position colored crosses so their arms align with matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross; Space switches between crosses. RULE: Dots must lie on the same-color cross’s horizontal or vertical line. TRAP: Thinking tips must touch dots; alignment anywhere on the arm works.

GOAL: Navigate to the green tile. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the player exactly two spaces in that direction. RULE: The player could only jump over empty floor, not walls or gaps. TRAP: Believing you could slide until hitting a wall, which caused you to overshoot targets and waste turns.

GOAL: Move the purple square from its starting spot to the white bar at the bottom. CONTROLS: Click the floating plus sign to teleport the square to its location. RULE: The plus sign reappears a fixed distance ahead after each move, creating a chain. TRAP: Clicking empty grid dots does nothing; you must wait for the plus to reappear.

GOAL: Adjust three white sections to match target widths using paired boundary controls. CONTROLS: Buttons above and below each bar shift adjacent boundaries in opposite directions. RULE: Total horizontal space is conserved; expanding one section shrinks its neighbor equally. TRAP: Assuming buttons always move boundaries visibly ignores limits; clicks blocking width-zero sections do nothing.

GOAL: Slide the block off the platform to clear the path. CONTROLS: Arrows steer the block; Space confirms the move. RULE: The block splits into two halves that travel diagonally down-left and down-right. TRAP: Assuming the block stays whole while sliding, rather than splitting upon impact.

GOAL: Set all pins to the down state to push the plug into the socket. CONTROLS: Click pin bars or stems to toggle their color between black and white. RULE: A pin with both bar and stem black moves the plug downward. TRAP: Assuming mixed black-and-white states move the plug; they actually move it sideways, missing the target.

GOAL: Align five shape slots to target glyphs within a strict action budget. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor horizontally; pressing UP or DOWN cycled the selected shape through a fixed sequence. RULE: Shapes cycled in a predictable order, allowing calculation of the shortest rotation path to the target. TRAP: Assuming DOWN always reverses the cycle wastes time; verifying the direction before batch-pressing prevents costly errors.

GOAL: Position the orange cross so its diagonal arms cover the target dot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the cross one step per press. RULE: A dot is collected only when an arm sweeps over it. TRAP: Assuming the cursor remains visible; it vanishes under other objects, requiring coordinate calculation instead of visual tracking.

GOAL: Rotate seven shapes to match targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor; UP rotates forward; DOWN rotates backward. RULE: All shapes follow one fixed cycle order; shortest path matters. TRAP: Assuming each shape has its own unique rotation sequence wastes moves; they share a global cycle.

GOAL: Raise three colored bars so their top segments align perfectly with the corresponding horizontal gaps in the grid. CONTROLS: Click the empty space above a bar to increase its height by one unit; click below or beside it to decrease. RULE: A bar is solved only when its top edge matches the gap row exactly; partial overlaps do not count as progress. TRAP: Assuming you could adjust multiple bars simultaneously or that overshooting a target was harmless; precise, single-unit adjustments were required.

GOAL: Match the blue row to the target by cycling shapes through cursor slots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; up and down buttons rotate the current shape. RULE: Each yellow shape corresponds to a specific blue shape sequence; segment yellow rows to deduce the blue target. TRAP: Assuming the blue cycle is simple; complex dependencies require precise segmentation of yellow tuples to find the unique blue solution.

GOAL: Guide three shifting shapes to collect glowing dots and fill empty boxes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: Only the current shape collects dots, so switch shapes to reach separate targets. TRAP: Thinking all shapes move at once wastes turns; you must switch to move each one individually.

GOAL: Reach the exit by crossing a lethal hazard without triggering its attack. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per turn. RULE: The hazard only attacks if you start your turn directly adjacent to it. TRAP: Avoid stepping onto the hazard's tile; passing through safely requires moving away before the turn ends.

ESTABLISHED: You can pick up the frame from below after stepping down, right, and up to face it. Carried frames pass through the bar. FAILED: Pressing UP while blocked does not reliably change your facing direction. GOAL IS NOT: Simply standing next to the frame or pressing SPACE from the side. CONTROLS: Arrows move and set facing. SPACE interacts in the facing direction.

GOAL: Move the frame to the upper slot and drop it. CONTROLS: Arrows move and face the player; Space grabs or drops objects. RULE: A blocked arrow still turns the player to face that direction. TRAP: Assuming blocked moves leave you facing the same way wastes turns adjusting position.

ESTABLISHED: Completing the green plus pattern resets the keypad and shrinks the key tip, indicating a failed attempt rather than a win. FAILED: Clicking whites or completing the pattern with the tip in the left orientation did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the plus shape on the keypad to the D-pad indicators. CONTROLS: Directional keys move the key tip; clicking keypad cells changes their color; completing the pattern triggers the reset penalty.

GOAL: Rotate the top row to match the target color sequence. CONTROLS: Up shifts colors forward; Down shifts colors backward. RULE: The cycle length is seven, so five Downs equal two Ups. TRAP: Assuming Down reverses the previous Up is wrong; it continues the cycle.

ESTABLISHED: Vertical pushes affect all blocks in the sweep's column range. FAILED: Pushing blocks up while others occupy the target band's columns. GOAL IS NOT: Moving blocks independently without considering vertical overlap. CONTROLS: Horizontal moves extend/retract the arm; vertical moves push all overlapping blocks.

GOAL: Cover every dot with a shape of the same color. CONTROLS: Arrows move shapes; Space rotates or toggles color state. RULE: A dot only counts if the covering shape’s color matches the dot’s color. TRAP: Assuming any shape covers any dot regardless of color; mismatched colors yield no progress.

GOAL: Clear the level by completing the plus shape and moving the tip to the far left. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; mouse clicks toggle keypad cells. RULE: The first click of the level triggers a tutorial animation and does nothing else. TRAP: Believing every click toggles a cell immediately, wasting an action when the initial tutorial consumes the first input.

GOAL: Reach the goal by navigating past hazards and capturing one enemy to clear a path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step per press; stepping on an enemy captures it. RULE: Hazards only attack directly in front of their facing dot; approaching from behind or the side is safe. TRAP: Believing all adjacent tiles are deadly; you must realize the rear and flanks are safe zones to bypass guards.

GOAL: Match the top color sequence by filling the middle slots with the correct palette colors. CONTROLS: Click a palette color to select it, then click a middle slot to place it. RULE: The top row dictates the required order; place colors left-to-right to match it. TRAP: Thinking you can place multiple colors with one selection; each slot requires a fresh click on the palette.

GOAL: Swap bars to align children with notches and clear paint bands. CONTROLS: Left/Right move platform, Mouse swaps bar, Space confirms. RULE: Matching widths allow children to fill notches without splashing. TRAP: Assuming bars block each other when overlapping in columns; they do not.

GOAL: Grow bars from dots to touch plus signs. CONTROLS: Click right glyph to extend green bar right; click bottom glyph to extend yellow bar down. RULE: Each click moves the bar end three units toward the target. TRAP: Thinking clicks move the dot itself; they actually extend the bar body, shifting the endpoint independently.

GOAL: Align the red entry and green exit markers to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click the arrows to rotate the ring; click the bracket to lock the position. RULE: The ring must rotate so the entry and exit colors match the block sequence. TRAP: Assuming clicks on empty space or static borders count toward the action limit.

GOAL: Clear the level by resolving all pluses. CONTROLS: Click a plus to select it, revealing a target marker; click another plus to resolve the pair. RULE: Selecting one plus highlights a corresponding target; clicking a second plus clears both the selection and the marker. TRAP: Clicking the marker cell directly does nothing; you must click another plus to trigger the clearing action.

GOAL: Reach the black exit box at the top of the corridor. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the sprite one step in that direction. RULE: Standing on the plus marker does not end the level; you must enter the exit. TRAP: The yellow bar is a real-time timer, not a move counter, so hesitation wastes time.

GOAL: Move the white piece to land the rope bead exactly on the ring center. CONTROLS: Click a black spot to move the white piece; the bead follows the rope’s midpoint. RULE: The bead sits halfway between the white piece and the anchor, so position carefully. TRAP: Assuming the bead moves directly to your click; it actually drags along, requiring precise positioning.

GOAL: Join the two blue squares so they touch, completing the key. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active square one step in that direction. RULE: The level ends only when the squares are adjacent, not just at the top. TRAP: Thinking you needed to reach specific corners or press Space delayed the simple touch.

GOAL: Match the grid pattern shown in the corner thumbnail. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle their color between blue and red. RULE: The thumbnail displays the target state, not the current state. TRAP: Assuming the thumbnail mirrors the grid; it actually reveals the solution.

GOAL: Match the 5x3 grid to the pattern shown by two overlapping 3x3 glyph maps. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle their color; click glyphs to inspect their mapped regions. RULE: Each glyph reveals a 3x3 section of the target image, with the glyph’s own color indicating the "ink" color to match. TRAP: Assuming glyphs show the final grid directly rather than distinct, overlapping map fragments.

GOAL: Slide the yellow pair into the target bracket positions. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows shift entire rows horizontally. RULE: Only the final position of the yellow tiles matters, not the rest of the grid. TRAP: Assuming row shifts move right when they actually move left, causing wasted clicks.

GOAL: Route a continuous chain from start to the plus symbol by extending and retracting colored segments. CONTROLS: Click buttons to extend or retract specific color segments; the chain head moves accordingly. RULE: Segments must connect end-to-end without overlapping occupied cells; a blocked extension halts progress. TRAP: Assuming you can extend any segment anytime; you must first retract the yellow body to clear the path before extending the orange.

GOAL: Swap two adjacent blocks using a single arrow press. CONTROLS: Arrows move blocks; the final press swaps their positions. RULE: Moving one block into the other’s space swaps them instantly. TRAP: Assuming you must move both blocks separately; one press does both.

ESTABLISHED: Green blocks have white dots. A purple gate exists. Moving blocks changes dot position. FAILED: Placing blocks on the frame, pushing against walls, and pressing directions on frame-adjacent blocks did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply covering the frame or touching the purple gate with a block. CONTROLS: Click to select a block. Arrow keys move the selected block one grid step.

GOAL: Sort colored tokens into matching red and green slots to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click a slot to pick up its token; click another to place it there. Space submits the current arrangement. RULE: Placing a token on a filled slot swaps them, leaving the displaced token in your hand for the next move. TRAP: Assuming you could drop a token into an empty slot to clear it; empty slots are only for final placement, not intermediate storage.

GOAL: Determine the correct color for each grid cell to form a consistent pattern. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color between red and orange. RULE: A block’s center color dictates its mapping: white pixels become the center color, gray pixels become the other. TRAP: Assuming block boundaries are simple rectangles; use the actual pixel data to find the true center and shape.

ESTABLISHED: The red plug tracks the player's horizontal position, clamping at column 16. The vertical corridor at column 16 remains blocked whenever the player approaches the descent point, as the plug follows within eighteen columns. FAILED: Moving the player right to pull the plug away from the corridor, then descending, failed because the plug re-engages the column 16 block as soon as the player moves left or down. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the bottom of the shaft. The objective is not merely traversing the vertical path, as the plug’s automatic tracking mechanism prevents direct descen

GOAL: Route yellow to the left bracket and orange to the right bracket by navigating them through two overlapping rings. CONTROLS: Click the left ring to rotate it counter-clockwise; click the right ring to rotate it clockwise. RULE: Rings share specific cells, so rotating one ring drags any token currently in those shared spots along with it. TRAP: Assuming the rings operate independently; ignoring that shared cells force simultaneous movement when one ring is turned.

GOAL: The player navigated a path while a ghost replayed their previous moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the character; Space reset the level to record a new ghost. RULE: A retractable barrier opened only when the ghost occupied the target socket location. TRAP: Believing the barrier depended on the player’s position caused failed descent attempts.

GOAL: Align the plug's prongs with the socket's red terminals to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug three units per press. RULE: Prong spacing must match terminal spacing for a successful connection. TRAP: Assuming a single-step movement causes overshooting; each press jumps three units, requiring precise counting.

GOAL: Move yellow and orange tokens to their target spots using cyclic shifts. CONTROLS: Red buttons shifted tokens vertically; green buttons shifted them horizontally. RULE: Tokens cycled through four distinct blocks, allowing transfer between paths at intersection cells. TRAP: Treating the board as a single grid ignores the block structure; tokens only move within their assigned cycle unless crossing a junction.

GOAL: Position the dark block inside the right frame. CONTROLS: Arrows push blocks; clicks select a block. RULE: Pushing a block sends it through walls, ignoring barriers. TRAP: Believing walls block all movement wastes time; pushed blocks pass through.

GOAL: Slide the black block so its reflection perfectly covers the yellow target shape. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to move the black block one step per press. RULE: The reflection mirrors across the center; only specific positions align the shapes. TRAP: Assuming the black block itself must match the yellow shape wastes time; focus on the mirrored image.

GOAL: Guide the two yellow tokens into the specific slots on the top row. CONTROLS: The top arrows shift the top row sideways, while the middle arrows rotate the entire grid in one long, winding loop. RULE: The middle arrow moves every token one step along a single continuous path that snakes through the whole board. TRAP: Thinking the middle arrow only affects nearby cells; it actually moves every token in a massive, connected chain.

GOAL: Paint the grid so overlapping glyph cells match their shared colors. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle colors through blue, red, and orange. RULE: A glyph’s center color marks its white cells; the other color marks its gray cells. TRAP: Assuming gray cells could vary per glyph; consistency forced them all to be red.

GOAL: Move three shapes to colored squares without touching multiple colors at once. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape one step; Space switches to the next shape. RULE: Only one color can be touched per move, so paths must avoid overlapping squares. TRAP: Trying to touch two squares in one move causes ambiguity; strict separation is required.

GOAL: Guide the player to the goal by managing two plugs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; Space launches a time-ghost replay of your previous moves. RULE: Plugs retract only while a character occupies their socket; they block movement when extended. TRAP: Assuming ghost replays ignore live obstacles or that plug retraction persists after leaving the socket.

GOAL: Align the black piece's reflection with the yellow target by moving the piece down and shifting the mirror divider. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active item; Space toggles between moving the piece and moving the divider. RULE: The reflection is a perfect horizontal mirror across the divider line; match the shape exactly. TRAP: Forgetting to switch modes wastes moves, as arrows control different objects depending on the current selection.

ESTABLISHED: Moving eats blue cells. Toggling swaps blue and dither. FAILED: Partial eating might break swap mechanics. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing all blue before swapping. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move and eat. Blue button triggers swap.

GOAL: Place three yellow blocks into their matching outer slots by rotating and expanding them. CONTROLS: Bottom arrow rotates the block counter-clockwise; right arrow expands the block’s distance from center. RULE: Each click changes one property only; count steps precisely to match the target arm and radius. TRAP: Assuming a single click handles both rotation and expansion wastes moves; treat them as separate actions.

GOAL: Reach the specific glyph pattern shown on the readout panels. CONTROLS: Clicking a plain cell toggles its state; clicking a mixed cell flips itself and its neighbors. RULE: Mixed cells act as multi-toggles, so solve them first to set the baseline before fixing plain cells. TRAP: Treating mixed cells as static or single-toggles causes endless loops; they affect adjacent cells too.

GOAL: Place two shapes onto matching yellow targets, then lift the central divider to reveal the reflections below. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active object; the spacebar cycles selection between the divider and the two pieces. RULE: The top bar tracks your step budget, turning consumed steps orange as you progress toward the limit. TRAP: Do not assume the black bar represents obstacles; it is actually a step counter that shifts color to indicate usage.

GOAL: Navigate the token through shifting red barriers to reach the yellow exit block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token; clicking the red podium toggles the barrier’s vertical position. RULE: The token consumes or passes through the barrier only when aligned with its current slot. TRAP: Assuming the barrier stays fixed; failing to toggle it before moving through the upper section blocks progress.

ESTABLISHED: Purple paint marks specific cells when pressed. Rotating changes the paint pattern. Some presses produce no visible change. FAILED: Pressing without rotating first does not clear the level. Repeated presses at the same orientation are redundant. GOAL IS NOT: Simply covering the entire block area with purple paint. CONTROLS: Left rotates the block. Space presses the stamp. Down does nothing.

ESTABLISHED: The plug is trapped in a room bounded by a solid wall to the left. A 3x3 grid of pluses sits beyond this wall, with the middle row adjacent to the room's ceiling level. FAILED: Climbing up through existing openings failed because the upper paths do not align with the plug's current horizontal position. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving left into the plus grid without destroying specific barriers is impossible; the wall does not open by touch alone. CONTROLS: Clicking a plus destroys it. Testing the middle-row plus is needed to see if it opens a path to the plug.

GOAL: Place two yellow items into specific target slots. CONTROLS: Blue clicks rotate rows; green clicks rotate columns; red arrows undo moves. RULE: Rotations affect entire lines, so moving one yellow often shifts the other. TRAP: Assuming moves are independent; ignoring the shared corner cell causes unintended swaps.

GOAL: Shrink the key's tip and slide it upward to insert it into the handle. CONTROLS: Click white keypad cells to shrink the tip; use arrow keys to move and rotate the key. RULE: The tip must be two units wide to fit into the handle's slot. TRAP: Believing the first action is wasted on a tutorial; here, clicks register immediately, so plan efficiently.

GOAL: Guide pieces into target cups by shifting them and lowering the divider. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles focus between the divider and pieces. RULE: Only the object with white dots responds to arrow keys; others stay still. TRAP: Assuming arrows move all pieces at once wastes moves; you must select each piece individually.

GOAL: Align prong tips to merge shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces; clicks rotate them. RULE: Fusions only occur when prong coordinates match exactly. TRAP: Assuming a shared bounding box implies a connection; it does not.

GOAL: Guide the plug to the pink target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the plug; clicks activated switches. RULE: The plug rises when its center aligns with an open channel. TRAP: Believing you could push the plug up; vertical movement is automatic only.

GOAL: Navigate two entities to plug sockets without colliding. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; spacebar confirms the setup. RULE: Lag behind the recording to ensure ghosts park before you arrive. TRAP: Assuming simultaneous arrival is safe; it causes blockage, so delay your entry.

GOAL: Guide the floating tip down a narrow shaft to insert it into the handle below. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the tip two units and rotate it ninety degrees in that direction. RULE: The tip must align horizontally with the handle’s opening to be absorbed upon contact. TRAP: Assuming rotation is optional; each move forces a turn, so you must track orientation to ensure the correct side faces the slot.

GOAL: Slide blocks into target zones using a tight action budget. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected blocks; clicks select new blocks. RULE: Every action, including selection, counts against the limit. TRAP: Assuming selection is free wastes actions; plan clicks carefully.

GOAL: Place tokens in parent and child boxes to satisfy linked faces. CONTROLS: Click palette to select token; click box slot to place; Space to confirm. RULE: Linked faces must match, but only specific slots accept input based on parent-child hierarchy. TRAP: Assuming all visible slots are clickable; one linked slot was locked, requiring tokens placed elsewhere to auto-fill it.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding a moving piston. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; the piston moves automatically each turn. RULE: The piston reverses direction instantly upon hitting a wall, never losing a turn. TRAP: Believing the piston pauses to turn wastes time; it moves continuously, so anticipate its immediate reversal.

GOAL: Cover all yellow cells using the piece and its mirror images. CONTROLS: Space cycles selection; arrows move the active piece or mirror axis. RULE: The solution only requires covering yellow areas, allowing extra cells to overlap. TRAP: Assuming exact coverage without overhang wastes time; allow overlaps to find the fit.

GOAL: Clear row 28 so the sky line could reach the target. CONTROLS: Clicks retracted the red bar upward and extended the sky line rightward. RULE: The red bar must sit below row 28 to keep the path open. TRAP: Assuming any retract length worked; moving too far pushed the attached horizontal bar into row 28, blocking the sky.

GOAL: Place a hollow connector to link the red box’s empty slot to the green box’s fixed shape. CONTROLS: Click to pick up the hollow piece and drop it into the target slot; press space to verify the solution. RULE: Fixed shapes cannot be moved but can be referenced by placing a matching connector piece in an empty linked slot. TRAP: Trying to click the pre-filled shape in the green box to move it wastes turns, as those tokens are locked in place.

GOAL: Align four movable objects to form a specific letter shape. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active object; Space cycles to the next object. RULE: Objects move in fixed three-cell steps, so only specific positions are reachable. TRAP: Assuming free movement wastes time; verify each target coordinate is a multiple of three from the start.

GOAL: Reach the bottom-right exit while avoiding moving pistons. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; timing is critical as pistons shift every turn. RULE: You must move against the piston's flow to survive, never stepping into its next position. TRAP: Assuming the shortest path works; taking the long way around prevents a fatal head-on collision with the returning piston.

GOAL: Move two Y-blocks into matching holes and place the G-block in the square frame. CONTROLS: Arrows move G; pushing Y-blocks shifts them fifteen units if space permits. RULE: G must align with a Y-block's arm to push it, requiring precise positioning between moves. TRAP: Assuming you can push a block multiple times without repositioning; each push needs a fresh approach.

GOAL: Align three shapes so their ends meet to form closed loops. CONTROLS: Click a shape to select it; arrow keys move the selected shape. RULE: Ends fuse only when they overlap exactly at the same grid point. TRAP: Moving one shape breaks existing fusions, forcing you to re-align others afterward.

GOAL: Sort tokens into matching color boxes to satisfy a repeating pattern. CONTROLS: Click a token to pick it up, then click a slot to place it; press Space to submit. RULE: The sequence must mirror a specific repeating structure, requiring connectors to bridge non-matching tokens. TRAP: Assuming placed tokens are locked; they are movable, so do not waste time trying to clear slots first.

GOAL: Rotate each tile until its glyph matches the target shape. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP and DOWN rotate the tile’s glyph cycle. RULE: P-tiles follow a fixed seven-glyph loop; calculate the shortest rotation distance to save actions. TRAP: Assuming all tiles share the same cycle wastes time; S-tiles have a separate, shorter cycle.

GOAL: Match colored tokens to boxes using hollow connectors. CONTROLS: Click palette items, click empty slots to place, press space to verify. RULE: Each box requires a specific connector shape and matching solid tokens in its slots. TRAP: Assuming any connector fits; only the hollow piece matching the box color works.

ESTABLISHED: Moving the white piece creates a bead that occludes the gray piece's center, blocking direct interaction. FAILED: Clicking the gray piece's center directly while occluded by the bead yields no result. GOAL IS NOT: Simply swapping pieces while the bead blocks the target cell. CONTROLS: Move the white piece to a distant cell first to shift the bead away, then swap the gray piece.

GOAL: Position the white diamond to clear the gray obstruction and reach the target. CONTROLS: Click a diamond to swap it with an adjacent one; drag a diamond to move it to an empty spot. RULE: Swaps only work if the clicked diamond is not fully hidden by the bead; drag first to reveal if needed. TRAP: Assuming you can click an occluded diamond; the bead blocks interaction, forcing an extra move to expose it.

GOAL: Place two mirrored shapes to cover all yellow blocks exactly. CONTROLS: Arrows moved pieces in three-cell steps; space confirmed the placement. RULE: Reflections off the grid are clipped, so edge pieces need not fit entirely inside. TRAP: Assuming pieces must stay fully on-board wasted time searching for impossible tight fits.

GOAL: Align all colored bars to their target heights using minimal moves. CONTROLS: Click a bar to extend it upward one unit per action. RULE: Bars grow from their fixed bottom anchor, pushing the top edge higher. TRAP: Assuming bars could slide horizontally or overlap; they only stretch vertically within their column.

GOAL: Guide the two-toned tip to the handle to absorb it. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; movement rotates its orientation. RULE: Absorption works regardless of which color faces the handle. TRAP: Assuming arrows rotate a fixed angle; rotation varies, so track position, not just facing.

GOAL: Deduce hidden slot identities to match the sequence pattern. CONTROLS: Click palette tokens, click board slots, press space to test. RULE: Flash outlines reveal which box expansion follows each connector. TRAP: Assuming the first connector links to the wrong box color.

GOAL: Guide the player to collect all red dots while navigating around moving pistons that temporarily block the path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in the cardinal direction. RULE: Red dots are permanent obstacles until collected; pistons pass over them, hiding them briefly but not destroying them. TRAP: Believing red dots disappear when a piston passes over them, leading to wasted time waiting for a respawn that never happens.

GOAL: Reach the exit tile by navigating a narrow, winding path through the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step in the chosen direction. RULE: You cannot pass through walls or blocked cells; the path is the only way. TRAP: Assuming a direct diagonal shortcut exists; it does not, forcing a longer detour.

GOAL: Guide the white bead to its destination by switching between green and purple ropes. CONTROLS: Click to move the white bead; click a colored slot to swap ropes. RULE: Swaps exchange rope identities instantly without moving bead positions, allowing precise midpoint calculations. TRAP: Assuming swaps physically move the bead or change slot locations wastes time; only rope affiliation changes.

GOAL: Guide three markers to their targets and align the square pair. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active marker; clicking a square selects the pair; clicking a marker selects it. RULE: Only the selected object moves; markers must be individually positioned before adjusting the squares. TRAP: Believing you can move all markers at once; you must click each marker to activate it.

GOAL: Reach the exit using six precise arrow presses. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player. RULE: You cannot stop on a tile once you enter it; you must keep moving until blocked. TRAP: Believing you can pause or reverse direction on a slide leads to overshooting the target and wasting moves.

ESTABLISHED: The platform occupies rows thirty-two to thirty-five, spanning columns zero through twenty-three. FAILED: Attempting to move the platform downward to rows forty-four to forty-seven without success. GOAL IS NOT: The objective is not to fill the lower sections or reach the bottom edge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the platform vertically; mouse clicks select specific grid cells to anchor movement.

GOAL: Clear Level 3 using a single action. CONTROLS: Spacebar completes the puzzle. RULE: Correct configuration requires no movement, only validation. TRAP: Believing you must physically move blocks to solve the level.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking destroys pluses. Right moves the plug. Destroying pluses opens paths for the plug to rise. FAILED: Precise coordinate calculations for pluses after scrolling caused wasted actions. Batching clicks without verifying the first result led to errors. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing all pluses. It is aligning the plug to rise through the socket into the upper region. CONTROLS: Click to destroy a plus. Right to move the plug.

ESTABLISHED: Two 2x2 pieces merge into a 3x3 piece when fully inside the ball. The 3x3 piece hangs partially off the bottom edge at rows 31-33. FAILED: Placing pieces partially inside the ball does not trigger a merge. Moving pieces without ensuring full containment wastes turns. GOAL IS NOT: Simply overlapping the ball with any piece. A single 3x3 piece alone does not clear the level. CONTROLS: Click and drag pieces to move them. Pieces merge automatically when conditions are met.

GOAL: Swap the positions of the two squares by crossing their paths. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected pair or marker; clicks toggle which one is active. RULE: Squares reset if blocked by the marker or walls, so clear a path first. TRAP: Thinking the marker moves vertically; it only shifts horizontally along the center row.

ESTABLISHED: Mode B makes row 1 pins push the plug down. Row 2 pins rotate or shift the plug left. Row 3 is inactive. The hole is above the plug. FAILED: Moving the plug downward. Rotating the plug. Shifting the plug horizontally without vertical gain. GOAL IS NOT: A puzzle where the plug moves only downward or sideways. CONTROLS: Left box sets mode A. Right box sets mode B. Pins apply effects in sequence. Run button executes the sequence.

ESTABLISHED: The red button rotates the red bar into a V shape. The pink V climb and yellow win zone are confirmed. FAILED: Guessing the step budget without measuring the W bar. Assuming the red button does nothing. GOAL IS NOT: A simple straight-line path. The red bar does not stay horizontal. CONTROLS: Clicking rotates the red bar. Moving costs steps. The W bar tracks remaining actions.

GOAL: Collect the prize by navigating the maze and activating the final switch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the character; clicking buttons rotated barriers. RULE: Barriers rotate ninety degrees when their switch is pressed, opening new paths. TRAP: Assuming the shortest path was viable; ignoring the switch required blocking your route until you circled back.

ESTABLISHED: The orange cell moves only in the outer track, never entering the panels. Panel pegs jump over adjacent pegs into empty spaces. FAILED: Positioning the orange cell adjacent to panel pegs did not allow interaction or transport. Placing one peg in each panel did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply having one peg in each panel, nor parking the orange cell at specific track coordinates. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the orange cell along the track; clicking pegs does not enable sliding or dragging.

ESTABLISHED: You are stuck against a frame. The orange holds a frame above the bar. FAILED: Moving directly into the frame does nothing; it blocks you without grabbing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply standing next to the frame or pushing it directly. CONTROLS: Movement sets facing. Space grabs a frame in front. To grab, move away, turn back, then Space.

ESTABLISHED: Water levels in tanks A, B, and C are stable at zero, eighteen, and thirty respectively. The floating block sits just above the water surface in tank A, outside the side window's vertical range. FAILED: Raising tank C's level to thirty-three did not trigger any water transfer through the connecting window to tank B, nor did it move the block. GOAL IS NOT: Simply maximizing tank C's volume or aligning the block's height with the window's top edge. CONTROLS: Clicking specific coordinates adjusts individual tank water levels by discrete increments, but does not directly move the bloc

GOAL: Rotate and translate the pad to align with the canvas. CONTROLS: Clicks rotate the pad; Space moves it. RULE: The pad must face the target and be positioned directly below it to paint upward. TRAP: Assuming rotation preserves the pad’s position; it pivots, shifting the pad and requiring recalculated translations.

GOAL: Fill the frame bar by placing five blocks into the assembly slots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; the Space key picks up or drops a block. RULE: Only one block can be held at a time, requiring precise routing to avoid collisions. TRAP: Assuming the automated helper stays out of the way; it often blocks the main path, forcing detours.

GOAL: Lift the plug sixteen rows to fill the overhead gap. CONTROLS: Click cells to set height modifiers; click Run to execute movement. RULE: Each column pair adds four units of upward force. TRAP: Assuming the plug could move sideways to align; it only moves straight up.

GOAL: Guide the token through a maze of colored blocks to reach the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token one block; mouse clicks activate switches or buttons. RULE: The token can only traverse blocks matching its current color state. TRAP: Assuming diagonal moves were allowed or that walls could be passed without matching colors caused wasted steps.

ESTABLISHED: Up and Down are the only valid moves here; Down from (30,14) works. FAILED: Moving Down from (35,14) does nothing; the path is blocked. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top; you must visit the plus sign three times before returning. CONTROLS: Up and Down move the sprite. Entering the plus sign from the North registers a press.

GOAL: Guide the plug from its starting spot to the yellow socket without rotating it. CONTROLS: Click the colored buttons to move the plug four spaces up, down, left, or right. RULE: The plug slides in straight lines of four spaces, stopping only when blocked by walls or the board edge. TRAP: Believing the plug needed to rotate to fit; it actually slid straight through the gap without turning.

GOAL: Guide two characters through separate rooms to collect keys that unlock shared doors, allowing final convergence in the top area. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one character; the other character moves in the opposite direction simultaneously. RULE: A door only opens when its matching key is held by the character currently standing on it. TRAP: Believing characters move independently; they are tethered, so every move for one forces a counter-move for the other.

GOAL: Move all frames into the container slots before the timer expires. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character; automatic moves trigger when near targets. RULE: Frames can only enter the container if the entry slot matches the frame's required position. TRAP: Assuming you can manually place frames anywhere; they must align with specific container rows to fit.

GOAL: Guide the arm to collect blocks by extending and retracting. CONTROLS: Arrows extend or retract the arm in four directions. RULE: Retraction pulls a block from the old tip position. TRAP: Assuming retraction pushes blocks away wastes moves.

GOAL: Move the ferry carrying a green peg to the bottom track, then jump it over a stationary peg into the final slot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys drive the ferry along its fixed wire path; mouse clicks select the ferry and designate the landing spot for the jump. RULE: The ferry strictly follows the black wire; it cannot leave the path or move diagonally. TRAP: Assuming the wire extends to the leftmost edge; the path actually stops at the second column, causing wasted moves trying to go further left.

GOAL: Place colored pads into matching canvas slots to fill target regions. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the pad to adjacent slots; Space presses the selected color. RULE: Left and Right keys rotate the pad clockwise along the circular track, regardless of position. TRAP: Assuming Left and Right rotate in opposite directions wastes time; both actually advance the angle clockwise.

GOAL: Align the player’s symbol with the target glyph to open the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; standing on a pad flips the symbol. RULE: The exit only unlocks when the displayed symbol exactly matches the door’s icon. TRAP: Assuming movement alone solves it; you must actively toggle the symbol to match, not just reach the door.
